result: The manuscript establishes that human cerebral organoids recapitulate key features of early brain development, including ventricular zone-like structures, gene expression programs, and epigenomic patterns of the fetal cortex, and have been used to model various neurodevelopmental disorders.
evaluation: Claims C1, C8-C14 are well-supported by extensive citations to prior work in the field. These claims establish the biological validity and utility of cerebral organoids as models for human brain development and disease, providing essential context for the current study.

result: Prior analyses of cerebral organoids have been limited to sectioned tissue or superficial layers due to high scattering properties and limitations of labeled imaging approaches.
evaluation: Claims C2, C29-C31 are supported by multiple citations to prior work and describe well-established technical limitations in the field. These claims establish the motivation for developing label-free deep tissue imaging methods.

result: Rett Syndrome is caused by MeCP2 mutations and is characterized by structural and functional deficits in human brains and mouse models, with 2D and 3D stem cell models revealing impaired proliferation, neuronal maturation, and migration deficits.
evaluation: Claims C15-C28 are well-supported by extensive citations to prior work characterizing RTT pathology in humans, mouse models, and stem cell models. These claims establish the biological context and prior knowledge about RTT that motivates the current investigation.

result: THG microscopy is a label-free imaging technique that generates signals at interfaces between aqueous and lipid-rich structures, has been applied to various tissues, and avoids phototoxicity and photobleaching problems.
evaluation: Claims C32-C33, C35-C38 are supported by citations to prior work and established physical principles of THG imaging. These claims establish the technical foundation and prior applications of THG microscopy that justify its use for organoid imaging.

result: The authors developed an optimized three-photon microscope with moderate repetition rate, reduced pulse width to 27 fs, and improved optical design that reduced average power requirements by 2-3 fold and increased signal collection by 2-fold compared to prior systems.
evaluation: Claims C42-C45, C88-C92 are supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 supplements 1-4. The technical optimizations are well-documented with measurements and comparisons to prior work. The claim of achieving <30 fs pulse widths for the first time (C90) is supported by the data but the novelty claim would require verification of the literature.

result: The optimized three-photon microscope enables label-free THG imaging of intact cerebral organoids to approximately 2 mm depth, limited only by the working distance of the objective.
evaluation: Claims C3 and C56 are supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2-3 and videos demonstrating imaging throughout the depth of organoids. The 2 mm depth capability is clearly demonstrated and represents a major technical achievement.

result: THG imaging of 35-day cerebral organoids reveals well-organized VZ and CP structures with distinct cell densities and morphologies, with THG signal arising from cell membranes and providing clear delineation between VZ (lower signal) and CP (higher signal) regions.
evaluation: Claims C46-C53 are supported by experimental data in Figure 2 showing immunostaining validation (KI67, TUJ1, DCX, 7AAD, WGA) alongside THG imaging. The correlation between THG signal patterns and known organoid structures is well-demonstrated.

result: GFP-labeled neurons in electroporated organoids show >85% overlap with THG signals in both WT and MT organoids, with 23/25 GFP+ cells in WT and 27/30 in MT organoids emitting somatic THG signals, and similar migration deficits observed with both labeling approaches.
evaluation: Claims C54-C55, C71-C73 are supported by experimental data in Figure 2 supplements 2-5 showing colocalization analysis. The high overlap percentages validate that THG signal reliably identifies neurons, supporting the use of label-free imaging for cell tracking.

result: Fixed WT organoids have an extinction length of 162.5 µm and MT organoids 148.2 µm at 1300 nm, making them at least 2× more scattering than mouse visual cortex, with WT organoids having significantly higher average extinction length (152.1±3.5 µm) than MT organoids (125.9±4.9 µm, p<0.005).
evaluation: Claims C57-C60 are supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 3C-E with appropriate statistical analysis (n=6 organoids, t-test). The extinction length measurements provide important characterization of the optical properties of organoids and differences between WT and MT.

result: RTT-MT organoids show slightly higher but non-significant VZ volume (p=0.3013), significantly higher VZ surface area (p<0.0001), significantly lower VZ thickness (p<0.0001), and significantly higher number of ventricles (p<0.0001) compared to RTT-WT organoids.
evaluation: Claims C61-C64, C39-C41, C4 are supported by experimental data in Figure 4 with appropriate statistical analysis (n=10 organoids, t-test) and data for individual lines shown in supplements. The 3D morphological analysis reveals significant structural differences in VZ organization between WT and MT organoids.

result: Live cell tracking reveals that RTT-WT neurons migrate at 23.4±0.2 µm/hr with straightness 0.881±0.004 and displacement 244.4±3.6 µm, while RTT-MT neurons show reduced speed (13.3±0.1 µm/hr), more tortuous trajectories (straightness 0.658±0.006), and shorter displacement (133.2±2.4 µm).
evaluation: Claims C65-C69, C5-C7 are supported by experimental data from live cell tracking in Figures 5-6 with substantial sample sizes (n=6 organoids, N=208 WT cells, N=217 MT cells). The migration deficits are consistent across multiple parameters and validated by comparison to prior work (C67). Statistical significance is clearly demonstrated.

result: Three-photon imaging of live organoids for up to 18 hours in the mini-incubator did not induce significant cell death compared to control organoids.
evaluation: Claim C70 is supported by Caspase3 immunostaining data in Figure 5 supplement 6 showing <2% Caspase3+ cells in both imaged and control organoids, compared to >10% in 90-day-old positive control organoids. This validates the biocompatibility of the imaging approach.

result: Two pairs of isogenic iPSC lines were used: Line 1 with MECP2 705delG frameshift mutation and Line 2 with MECP2 R306C mutation (which blocks NCoR/SMRT interaction), with WT lines expressing only wild-type allele and MT lines expressing only mutant allele due to X-inactivation.
evaluation: Claims C93-C97 are supported by citations to prior work describing the generation and characterization of these cell lines (Mellios et al., 2011; Nott et al., 2016). The use of isogenic pairs controls for genetic background and strengthens the experimental design.

result: Incubation of fixed organoids in H-protos index-matching solution for 3 hours improved maximum imaging depth by up to 50% compared to organoids without incubation.
evaluation: Claim C98 is supported by experimental data in Figure 5 supplement 7 showing depth improvements in 40% (4/10) of organoids tested. This demonstrates an optional enhancement to the imaging protocol, though it was not used for all experiments.

result: VZ expansion is uniquely different in human versus mouse neurogenesis, suggesting that the VZ phenotype observed in RTT organoids would likely go unobserved in mouse models of RTT.
evaluation: Claims C74-C75 are supported by citation to prior work (Florio and Huttner, 2014) on species differences in neurogenesis. The inference that mouse models would miss this phenotype (C75) is reasonable given the known differences in VZ expansion between species, though it remains speculative without direct testing.

result: Prior studies suggested impaired migration in RTT models, and the current findings show that lower migration speed and tortuous patterns are common in MT organoids regardless of radial thickness variation.
evaluation: Claims C76-C77 are supported by citations to prior work (Mellios et al., 2011; Bedogni et al., 2016) and by the experimental observations across multiple MT organoids shown in Figure 5 supplement 3. The consistency of migration deficits across organoids with varying thickness strengthens the findings.

result: Altered cytoskeleton dynamics and non-cell autonomous effects such as impaired cell-to-cell communication, adhesion, and radial glia dysfunction could contribute to the observed migration defects in RTT.
evaluation: Claims C78-C79 are speculative mechanistic hypotheses supported by citations to prior work on cytoskeletal defects (C78) but not directly tested in the current study. These represent reasonable hypotheses for future investigation but are not demonstrated by the current data.

result: Changes in ventricular wall thickness result from both decreased neurogenesis/increased proliferation and abnormally slow displacement and tortuous trajectories of neurons, providing insight into previously described deficits in human RTT brains.
evaluation: Claims C80-C81 represent integrative conclusions connecting the VZ structural deficits (Figure 4) with the migration deficits (Figures 5-6) and relating them to prior observations in RTT patients. The inference is well-supported by the combination of findings, though the connection to human pathology remains indirect.

result: The optimized three-photon microscopy system could provide a platform for monitoring abnormalities in organoids from patients with neurogenetic disorders, therapeutic drug screening, studying calcium dynamics, imaging myelinated axons and vasculature for MS/Alzheimer's research, and cancer applications.
evaluation: Claims C82-C87 are speculative statements about potential future applications of the technology. While the technical capabilities demonstrated in the current work support these possibilities, none of these applications are actually demonstrated in the manuscript. These represent reasonable future directions but are not validated results.
